alex: heads up — noticed a p99/p999 tail bump on Mixtral MoE after last night's kernel rollout. observed at ~03:10 UTC in prod :eyes:
maria: ugh, saw that in the dashboard. p99 jumped from 120ms -> 310ms on routing-heavy traces
sam_k: quick summary from profiling: router logits compute stayed same, but end-to-end tail is coming from a sudden KV cache miss storm and expert queueing spikes
jen_l: can you paste the sample trace? any stack skew to a new kernel path?
alex: snippet from flamegraph (cropped):
```
mixtral::router::compute_logits
mixtral::routing::topk_select
runtime::kernel::mixed_attention_fastpath  <-- unchanged
runtime::kernel::kv_cache_fetch  <-- 49% more time
runtime::scheduler::expert_enqueue
```

maria: interesting — kv_cache_fetch latency up + expert_enqueue waiting. that suggests cache eviction/pressure causing long tail, not pure routing math
sam_k: i ran `perf record` on a stressed node (same config as prod fast-path):
```
Kernel v2.14.7 -> introduced a micro-opt in kernel scheduler (better batching for dense attention)
perf top shows: kernel_scheduler_lock contention up, kv cache read latency up 3-4x under load
```

perf-bot: alert: mixtral-prod cluster alpha-10 p99 latency = 310ms (baseline 120ms). recent deploy: runtime-kernel@v2.14.7 (deployed 02:55 UTC)
jen_l: rolling back kernel is the blunt option. what about software mitigations? temporary knobs we can flip? :thinking:
alex: yes — suggested short-term mitigations: 1) reduce router top-k from 5->3 for high-concurrency routes (cuts expert fanout) 2) enable soft-topk (probabilistic top-k shrink) for low-confidence logits 3) raise per-expert inflight limit to allow smaller queues but faster churn 4) increase KV cache TTL/window for shared prefixes to avoid thrash
maria: can we do A/B on a canary pool? also need to watch quality regressions if top-k lowered (might change output). I'll run a small eval set against topk=3/soft-topk to check deltas
sam_k: implementing soft-topk will need router change + policy flag. quick patch: if max_logit_delta < 0.2 -> use topk=min(3, K) else topk=K. prototype in `router/policy/soft_topk.cpp` — cheap and safe for rollback
alex: i also noticed RoPE scaling interactions: longer sequences showed disproportionate KV misses because rope-sliced cache keys grow wider and evict hot expert keys faster. hypothesis: RoPE scaling -> bigger key fingerprints -> cache fragmentation under our LRU profile
jen_l: hmm — so quantized kernel change + longer RoPE sequences = more cache churn. makes sense. what about adjusting cache shard policy?
maria: we can try split caches by sequence-length buckets (short/medium/long) so long sequences don't evict short-sequence hot keys. low effort: add `seq_len_bucket` to cache key prefix and test on canary
perf-bot: suggested experiment created: experiment/2678904321-soft-topk-canary (targets alpha-10/alpha-12)
sam_k: performance sim results on test harness (100k requests):
- baseline v2.14.6, topk=5: p99=115ms, kv-hit=92%
- v2.14.7, topk=5: p99=308ms, kv-hit=71%
- v2.14.7, topk=3: p99=138ms, kv-hit=75%
- v2.14.7, topk=3 + seq-bucketed-cache: p99=122ms, kv-hit=90%
so lowering topk recovers some tail, but combined cache bucketing recovers hit-rate and overall latency
jen_l: these numbers look promising. what's the risk surface? any model-quality regression?
maria: initial eval on our regen set: topk=3 causes 0.7% drop in ppl on a small prompt slice and some diversity loss on creative prompts. with soft-topk (probabilistic) the quality delta is ~0.2% — acceptable as a temporary mitigation
alex: action items:
- maria -> run full eval (A/B) against production prompt corpus and generate rollback criteria (due EOD)
- sam_k -> instrument router to enable soft-topk flag and seq_len_bucketed cache (PR draft in about 90m)
- jen_l -> prepare canary rollout plan + monitoring alert tweak (p99 and kv-hit per-expert)
- alex -> block / revert kernel if experiments fail to hit 80% of baseline p99 within 2 hours of canary
jen_l: i'll also open an infra ticket to trace kernel_scheduler_lock perf counters into our observability stack (need histograms of lock hold times)
perf-bot: ticket created: INT-7783 (kernel lock histogram + perf counters)
alex: one more note — consider tuning expert parallelism: for heavily skewed hotset loads, increasing expert parallelism (more shards per expert) reduces single-expert queueing but increases KV footprint. tradeoff tradeoff. we'll include a param sweep in the canary
maria: agreed. include expert_parallelism={1,2,4} in the experiment matrix. Sam — can your harness simulate skewed hotsets?
sam_k: yes — adding two hotset patterns: (a) concentrated single hot expert, (b) medium hotspot across 3 experts. will run tonight and post results in the thread
jen_l: ok, plan looks solid. if canary numbers match the sim (p99 ~ baseline and kv-hit >85%) we push soft-topk+seq-buckets to prod and hold kernel rollout until kernel v2.14.7 is investigated
alex: thanks all. please ping here with PRs + canary link. i'll coordinate with oncall for possible rollback window. :v:
